Topics · Death and what comes after

How could bones and dust live again?

The Quran records the objection, then walks from your existence to the earth after rain. You conclude.

Part 1 of 4

﴿وَضَرَبَ لَنَا مَثَلًا وَنَسِىَ خَلْقَهُۥ ۖ قَالَ مَن يُحْىِ ٱلْعِظَـٰمَ وَهِىَ رَمِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And he presents for Us an example[1284] and forgets his [own] creation. He says, "Who will give life to bones while they are disintegrated?"

Translator's notes

[1284] Attempting to establish the finality of death.

Quran · Ya-Sin 36:78

Translation

As it is written, “I have made you a father of many nations.” This is in the presence of him whom he believed: God, who gives life to the dead, and calls the things that are not, as though they were. Against hope, Abraham in hope believed, to the end that he might become a father of many nations, according to that which had been spoken, “So will your offspring be.” Without being weakened in faith, he didn’t consider his own body, already having been worn out, (he being about a hundred years old), and the deadness of Sarah’s womb. Yet, looking to the promise of God, he didn’t waver through unbelief, but grew strong through faith, giving glory to God, and being fully assured that what he had promised, he was also able to perform.

Original · Ancient Greek

καθὼς γέγραπται ὅτι Πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν τέθεικά σε), κατέναντι οὗ ἐπίστευσεν θεοῦ τοῦ ζῳοποιοῦντος τοὺς νεκροὺς καὶ καλοῦντος τὰ μὴ ὄντα ὡς ὄντα· ὃς παρʼ ἐλπίδα ἐπʼ ἐλπίδι ἐπίστευσεν εἰς τὸ γενέσθαι αὐτὸν πατέρα πολλῶν ἐθνῶν κατὰ τὸ εἰρημένον· Οὕτως ἔσται τὸ σπέρμα σου· καὶ μὴ ἀσθενήσας τῇ πίστει κατενόησεν τὸ ἑαυτοῦ σῶμα νενεκρωμένον, ἑκατονταετής που ὑπάρχων, καὶ τὴν νέκρωσιν τῆς μήτρας Σάρρας, εἰς δὲ τὴν ἐπαγγελίαν τοῦ θεοῦ οὐ διεκρίθη τῇ ἀπιστίᾳ ἀλλὰ ἐνεδυναμώθη τῇ πίστει, δοὺς δόξαν τῷ θεῷ καὶ πληροφορηθεὶς ὅτι ὃ ἐπήγγελται δυνατός ἐστιν καὶ ποιῆσαι.

Romans · 4:17-21

World English Bible

Before any answer, the objection itself is recorded. A man asks who could possibly bring crumbled bones to life. The verse does not call him a fool for asking; it quotes him. So the question you have is one the Quran chose to carry inside itself, and it adds one observation: he has forgotten how he himself was made. Keep that observation; the argument will stand on it.

A question for you

Which is closest to your own doubt?

If you sayBones that are dust cannot come back.
ThenThat is the questioner's exact objection. The next parts answer it on its own terms.
If you sayNo one has ever come back.
ThenFair. The argument will not ask you to believe a report; it will ask what you already know about how you came to exist.
If you sayI see no reason it would happen.
ThenThen the question of purpose matters to you. Hold it; a later Step takes it up.

Part 2 of 4

﴿أَمْ خُلِقُوا۟ مِنْ غَيْرِ شَىْءٍ أَمْ هُمُ ٱلْخَـٰلِقُونَ٣٥ أَمْ خَلَقُوا۟ ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضَ ۚ بَل لَّا يُوقِنُونَ٣٦﴾

Translation of the meaning

Or were they created by nothing, or were they the creators [of themselves]? Or did they create the heavens and the earth? Rather, they are not certain.

Quran · At-Tur 52:35-36

Translation

I beg you, my child, to lift your eyes to the sky and the earth, and to see all things that are in it, and thus to recognize that God made them not of things that were, and that the race of men in this way comes into being.

Original · Ancient Greek

Ἀξιῶ σε, τέκνον, ἀναβλέψαντα εἰς τὸν οὐρανὸν καὶ τὴν γῆν, καὶ τὰ ἐν αὐτοῖς πάντα ἰδόντα, γνῶναι ὅτι ἐξ οὐκ ὄντων ἐποίησεν αὐτὰ ὁ Θεὸς, καὶ τὸ τῶν ἀνθρώπων γένος οὕτως γεγένηται,

2 Maccabees · 7:28

World English Bible

Set resurrection aside and start with your own existence, which neither of us doubts. How did it come about? From nothing, from yourself, or from a maker. Your parents and nature are real links, but they move the question back a step and do not end it. The verses name the first two and ask whether either is true of you. If neither is, the third is not a belief you are being asked to add; it is what the verses leave standing.

A question for you

Which is true of you?

If you sayI came from nothing.
ThenThen nothing produced bone, blood and a mind that asks questions. The verse leaves you to weigh whether that is the easier claim.
If you sayI made myself.
ThenThen you would remember doing it, and you would have been there before you were. The verse leaves this with you.
If you saySomething made me.
ThenThat is the third option, the one the verses leave unsaid for you to say. Keep it; the next part builds on it.

Part 3 of 4

﴿قُلْ يُحْيِيهَا ٱلَّذِىٓ أَنشَأَهَآ أَوَّلَ مَرَّةٍ ۖ وَهُوَ بِكُلِّ خَلْقٍ عَلِيمٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

Say, "He will give them life who produced them the first time; and He is, of all creation, Knowing."

Quran · Ya-Sin 36:79

Translation

“I don’t know how you came into my womb. It wasn’t I who gave you your spirit and your life. It wasn’t I who brought into order the first elements of each one of you. Therefore the Creator of the world, who shaped the first origin of man and devised the first origin of all things, in mercy gives back to you again both your spirit and your life, as you now treat yourselves with contempt for his laws’ sake.”

Original · Ancient Greek

οὐδʼ οἶδʼ ὅπως εἰς τὴν ἐμὴν ἐφάνητε κοιλίαν, οὐδὲ ἐγὼ τὸ πνεῦμα καὶ τὴν ζωὴν ὑμῖν ἐχαρισάμην, καὶ τὴν ἑκάστου στοιχείωσιν οὐκ ἐγὼ διερύθμισα. Τοιγαροῦν ὁ τοῦ κόσμου κτίστης ὁ πλάσας ἀνθρώπου γένεσιν, καὶ πάντων ἐξευρὼν γένεσιν, καὶ τὸ πνεῦμα καὶ τὴν ζωὴν ὑμῖν πάλιν ἀποδώσει μετʼ ἐλέους, ὡς νῦν ὑπερορᾶτε ἑαυτοὺς διὰ τοὺς αὐτοῦνόμους.

2 Maccabees · 7:22-23

World English Bible

﴿وَهُوَ ٱلَّذِى يَبْدَؤُا۟ ٱلْخَلْقَ ثُمَّ يُعِيدُهُۥ وَهُوَ أَهْوَنُ عَلَيْهِ ۚ وَلَهُ ٱلْمَثَلُ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ فِى ٱلسَّمَـٰوَٰتِ وَٱلْأَرْضِ ۚ وَهُوَ ٱلْعَزِيزُ ٱلْحَكِيمُ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And it is He who begins creation; then He repeats it, and that is [even] easier for Him. To Him belongs the highest description [i.e., attribute] in the heavens and earth. And He is the Exalted in Might, the Wise.

Quran · Ar-Rum 30:27

Grant for a moment that someone who knows made you the first time. Then that maker knew where every bone goes, having put them there. A repeat is not a new problem for whoever solved the first one; the second verse says it is the easier of the two. This shows the repeat is possible. That it will happen is the verse's promise, and weighing a promise means weighing the one who makes it.

A question for you

Which is harder?

If you sayThe first making.
ThenThen the repeat, by your own measure, is the lesser task. That is the verse's point exactly.
If you sayThe repeat.
ThenThen ask what would make it harder for one who already knows every part. The verse's answer is that nothing does.
If you sayThe same.
ThenThen whoever did the first can do the second. The verse only adds that the second is easier.

Part 4 of 4

﴿وَمِنْ ءَايَـٰتِهِۦٓ أَنَّكَ تَرَى ٱلْأَرْضَ خَـٰشِعَةً فَإِذَآ أَنزَلْنَا عَلَيْهَا ٱلْمَآءَ ٱهْتَزَّتْ وَرَبَتْ ۚ إِنَّ ٱلَّذِىٓ أَحْيَاهَا لَمُحْىِ ٱلْمَوْتَىٰٓ ۚ إِنَّهُۥ عَلَىٰ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ قَدِيرٌ﴾

Translation of the meaning

And of His signs is that you see the earth stilled, but when We send down upon it rain, it quivers and grows. Indeed, He who has given it life is the Giver of Life to the dead. Indeed, He is over all things competent.

Quran · Fussilat 41:39

Translation

Who has cut a channel for the flood water, or the path for the thunderstorm, to cause it to rain on a land where there is no man, on the wilderness, in which there is no man, to satisfy the waste and desolate ground, to cause the tender grass to grow?

Original · Hebrew

מִֽי־פִלַּ֣ג לַשֶּׁ֣טֶף תְּעָלָ֑ה וְ֝דֶ֗רֶךְ לַחֲזִ֥יז קֹלֽוֹת׃ לְ֭הַמְטִיר עַל־אֶ֣רֶץ לֹא־אִ֑ישׁ מִ֝דְבָּ֗ר לֹא־אָדָ֥ם בּֽוֹ׃ לְהַשְׂבִּ֣יעַ שֹׁ֭אָה וּמְשֹׁאָ֑ה וּ֝לְהַצְמִ֗יחַ מֹ֣צָא דֶֽשֶׁא׃

Job · 38:25-27

World English Bible

An argument from analogy, offered as an observation you can check. Land that is dry and still, then rain, then it stirs and swells. The verse draws one line from that to the dead: the one who does the first does the second. It does not say the two are the same; it says the same power is at work, and you have seen half of it.

A question for you

Have you watched dry land turn green after rain?

If you sayYes.
ThenThen you have seen the half of the argument that can be seen.
If you sayNot that I noticed.
ThenThen watch for it. The verse is content to wait for the next rain.

The same in the other books

Translation

Know that Yahweh, he is God. It is he who has made us, and we are his. We are his people, and the sheep of his pasture.

the Psalms · 100:3
